'''''Asplenium aethiopicum''''' is a [[Lithophyte|lithophytic]] or sometimes [[Epiphyte|epiphytic]] [[species]] of [[fern]] found in Southern and tropical Africa, tropical America, Asia and Australia.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Brownsey |first=P.J. |author-link=Patrick Brownsey |date=2020 |title=Asplenium aethiopicum v. 7 |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Asplenium%20aethiopicum |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=Flora of Australia}}</ref><ref name="inaturalist-Asplenium aethiopicum">{{cite web |title=Asplenium aethiopicum |url=https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/142831-Asplenium-aethiopicum |website=iNaturalist |access-date=2024-07-15 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=VicFlora: Asplenium aethiopicum |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/00c41030-8983-4126-8b57-2a32fe559089 |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au}}</ref> It is listed as critically endangered in [[Victoria (state)|Victoria]], Australia.<ref name=":1" /> It is considered exotic in New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Flora of New Zealand {{!}} Taxon Profile {{!}} Asplenium aethiopicum |url=https://www.nzflora.info/factsheet/taxon/Asplenium-aethiopicum.html |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=www.nzflora.info}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
''Asplenium aethiopicum'' was originally published under the name ''Trichomanes aethiopicum'' by [[Nicolaas Laurens Burman]] in 1768.<ref name=":0" /> In 1935 Alfred Becherer moved this taxon to the genus ''Asplenium'' creating the name ''Asplenium aethiopicum''.<ref name=":0" />
